questions.prompt: What does Lindy mean in Taleb’s frame?
choices: That all old things are automatically good
That endurance under time is a credibility signal in uncertain domains
That novelty should always be rejected

explanation.gentle: Lindy treats survival across time as meaningful evidence.
explanation.direct: Taleb uses endurance as a trust signal under uncertainty.
explanation.competitive: What survives longer has already passed tests the new thing has not.

questions.prompt: Why does Taleb give extra weight to what has endured longer?
choices: Because time guarantees perfection
Because survival reflects many hidden encounters with stress and selection
Because old things are always sacred

explanation.gentle: Time-tested things have already faced many chances to fail.
explanation.direct: Endurance records hidden selection pressures newer things have not yet seen.
explanation.competitive: The survivor already took punches the rookie has not.

questions.prompt: How does Lindy differ from blind conservatism?
choices: It worships every tradition equally
It treats durability as evidence without claiming old things are automatically right
It rejects all innovation

explanation.gentle: Taleb is rewarding endurance, not age by itself.
explanation.direct: Lindy raises default trust for survivors without turning them into saints.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 8 fit after the earlier chapters on downside and legitimacy?
choices: Because it abandons those themes
Because time becomes another realism filter showing what has already been exposed to the world
Because it moves away from credibility entirely

explanation.gentle: Lindy adds time to the book’s other exposure tests.
explanation.direct: The chapter extends Taleb’s trust logic by treating duration as another kind of contact with reality.
explanation.competitive: After friction and pain comes the longest beating: time.

questions.prompt: A new method looks exciting but has no long track record, while an older method has survived repeated stress. What is the most Taleb-like reading?
choices: The new method should always replace the old one
The older method deserves more default trust until the newcomer survives enough testing
The older method must be perfect

explanation.gentle: The durable method has already passed more silent tests.
explanation.direct: Taleb shifts the burden of proof toward the untested newcomer.
explanation.competitive: Do not promote the rookie over the scarred veteran too quickly.

questions.prompt: What does Taleb mean by saying time is an expert?
choices: Time makes every survivor morally good
Time filters fragile things out and leaves endurance as evidence
Time replaces all other forms of judgment

explanation.gentle: Time has already done a lot of silent selection work.
explanation.direct: The point is that survival under duration reveals something about fragility and resilience.
explanation.competitive: Time keeps a graveyard of weak claims and a shortlist of survivors.

questions.prompt: Why does novelty carry a higher burden of proof in this chapter?
choices: Because new things are always bad
Because recency often means less information about how the thing behaves under stress
Because institutions dislike change

explanation.gentle: The new thing has not yet survived enough reality.
explanation.direct: Taleb treats recency as missing evidence, not as automatic superiority.

questions.prompt: What should you ask when choosing between a durable option and a fashionable new one under uncertainty?
choices: Which one sounds more modern
Which one has already survived more hidden testing over time
Which one has the better branding

explanation.gentle: Time-tested endurance is a key signal in this chapter.
explanation.direct: The right question is how much temporal stress each option has already faced.
explanation.competitive: Ask who has already been beaten on by time and stayed up.

questions.prompt: How does Lindy change default trust allocation?
choices: It makes old things beyond criticism
It gives durable things a stronger starting presumption without ending scrutiny
It removes the need for experimentation

explanation.gentle: The survivor gets more default trust, not a blank check.
explanation.direct: Taleb raises prior credibility for the time-tested while preserving judgment.
explanation.competitive: The scar earns a head start, not sainthood.

questions.prompt: What larger lesson about uncertainty is Chapter 8 teaching?
choices: That theory should replace survival evidence
That endurance under time can reveal robustness where formal certainty is weak
That hype is a better guide than history

explanation.gentle: Time can reveal what formal confidence misses in uncertain settings.
explanation.direct: Taleb is teaching that survival is meaningful evidence when prediction is limited.
explanation.competitive: When certainty is cheap, trust the thing that already survived the beatings.
